subproblem.title: Density one of H^n on a set covered by closed Lipschitz graphs of arbitrarily small slope
subproblem.statement: Let A ⊆ ℝ^N with H^n(A) < ∞ and A H^n-null-measurable, and suppose that for every L ∈ (0,1] there is a countable set C_L ⊆ G(N,n) × 2^{ℝ^N} such that every (P, Γ) ∈ C_L has Γ closed and an L-graph over P (|q_P(y − z)| ≤ L|p_P(y − z)| on Γ), and A ⊆ ⋃_{(P,Γ) ∈ C_L} Γ. Let λ := H^n⌞A. Then for λ-a.e. x, λ(B_r(x))/(ω_n r^n) → 1 as r ↓ 0, i.e. HasDensity n λ x 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclidean N)), μHE[n] A ≠ ∞ → NullMeasurableSet A μHE[n] → (∀ L : ℝ, 0 < L → L ≤ 1 → ∃ C : Set (Grassmannian N n × Set (Euclidean N)), C.Countable ∧ (∀ c ∈ C, IsClosed c.2 ∧ ∀ y ∈ c.2, ∀ z ∈ c.2, ‖(y - z) - Grassmannian.project c.1 (y - z)‖ ≤ L * ‖Grassmannian.project c.1 (y - z)‖) ∧ A ⊆ ⋃ c ∈ C, c.2) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict A, HasDensity n ((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict A) x 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 of the parent proof of Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2. It supplies the density-one property of H^n on a rectifiable carrier (the part of Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 ⇒ / Remark 1.5(3) used through "1.9 of Ch. 3") directly from Lipschitz graphs of arbitrarily small slope, using only Lipschitz image bounds for H^n and the Lebesgue density theorem (no area formula). Notation: H^n := μHE[n] (= c_n · μH[n] for a constant c_n ∈ (0, ∞), Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def); ℝ^n := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure L^n := volume; ω := unitBallVolume n = L^n(ball 0 1) ∈ (0, ∞); B_r(y) := closedBall y r; λ := H^n.restrict A; for P ∈ G := Grassmannian N n, p_P := Grassmannian.project P; densityRatio n λ x r = λ(B_r(x))/(ω · ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n).

0. λ(ℝ^N) = H^n(A) < ∞, so λ is a finite, hence locally finite, Borel measure. Since A is H^n-null-measurable, λ-a.e. point lies in A (ae_restrict_mem₀).

1. Case n = 0. μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero), μH[0]{a} = 1 (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton), and finite sets are Borel, so H^0(F) = #F for every finite F ⊆ ℝ^N; if A were infinite it would contain finite subsets of every cardinality, contradicting H^0(A) < ∞. Hence A is finite. Moreover ω = unitBallVolume 0 = 1: ball 0 1 is the whole zero-dimensional space and volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 0) is the Dirac mass at 0 (Mathlib volume_euclideanSpace_eq_dirac). For x ∈ A choose r_x > 0 smaller than the distance from x to every other point of A (r_x := 1 if A = {x}); for 0 < r < r_x, λ(B_r(x)) = H^0(A ∩ B_r(x)) = H^0({x}) = 1 (Measure.restrict_apply, B_r(x) closed), so densityRatio 0 λ x r = 1/(1 · 1) = 1. Thus HasDensity 0 λ x 1 for every x ∈ A, hence for λ-a.e. x by 0. From now on n ≥ 1.

2. Graph geometry. Fix L ∈ (0, 1], c = (P, Γ) ∈ C_L, p := p_P and β := (1 + L²)^{1/2}. projectionLinearMap P is symmetric and idempotent, so |v|² = |p v|² + |v − p v|² and |p v| ≤ |v|; hence for y, z ∈ Γ: |p y − p z| ≤ |y − z| and |y − z|² = |p(y − z)|² + |(y − z) − p(y − z)|² ≤ (1 + L²)|p y − p z|², i.e. |y − z| ≤ β |p y − p z|. So p is injective on Γ, and h := Function.invFunOn p Γ satisfies h(p y) = y on Γ and is β-Lipschitz on p(Γ). Put A_c := A ∩ Γ.

3. Comparison with the projection. Let x ∈ A_c, r > 0 and s := r/β. Then (a) p(A_c) ∩ B_s(p x) ⊆ p(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) ⊆ p(A_c) ∩ B_r(p x) [if a = p z with z ∈ A_c and |a − p x| ≤ s, then |z − x| ≤ β s = r; conversely |p z − p x| ≤ |z − x|], and (b) A_c ∩ B_r(x) = h(p(A_c ∩ B_r(x))). H^n does not increase under the 1-Lipschitz map p and increases at most by the factor β^n under h, which is β-Lipschitz on p(Γ) ⊇ p(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) (Mathlib LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le and LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, MeasureTheory/Measure/Hausdorff.lean:745 and 733, valid for arbitrary sets; they transfer to μHE[n] through the constant c_n). Therefore
 (∗) H^n(p(A_c) ∩ B_s(p x)) ≤ H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ β^n H^n(p(A_c) ∩ B_r(p x)).

4. Lebesgue density in the plane. Let e : ℝ^n ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] P.plane be a linear isometry equivalence (finrank P.plane = n, Grassmannian.finrank_plane) and ι := Subtype.val ∘ e, an isometry ℝ^n → ℝ^N with range P.plane. For every B ⊆ ℝ^n, H^n(ι(B)) = L^n(B) (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Mathlib Geometry/Euclidean/Volume/Measure.lean:131 and 187). Put S := ι⁻¹(p(A_c)); since p(A_c) ⊆ P.plane = range ι we have ι(S) = p(A_c), and for b ∈ ℝ^n and s > 0, ι(S ∩ B_s(b)) = p(A_c) ∩ B_s(ι b) (ι is injective, isometric and onto P.plane); hence H^n(p(A_c) ∩ B_s(ι b)) = L^n(S ∩ B_s(b)), while L^n(B_s(b)) = ω s^n (Measure.addHaar_closedBall). By the Lebesgue density theorem for arbitrary sets (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for L^n and S, Covering/Besicovitch.lean:1105), L^n(S ∩ B_s(b))/L^n(B_s(b)) → 1 as s ↓ 0 for (L^n.restrict S)-a.e. b; choose a Borel set E ⊆ ℝ^n containing all exceptional points with (L^n.restrict S)(E) = L^n(E ∩ S) = 0. Let N_c := ι(E ∩ S) ⊆ p(A_c). Then H^n(N_c) = L^n(E ∩ S) = 0, and for every a ∈ p(A_c) ∖ N_c (a = ι b with b ∈ S ∖ E): H^n(p(A_c) ∩ B_s(a))/(ω s^n) → 1 as s ↓ 0. Finally X_c := {x ∈ A_c : p x ∈ N_c} ⊆ h(N_c), so H^n(X_c) ≤ β^n H^n(N_c) = 0.

5. Two-sided bounds. Let x ∈ A_c ∖ X_c; then a := p x ∈ p(A_c) ∖ N_c, and by (∗) and 4 (with s = r/β, so ω s^n = β^{−n} ω r^n):
 liminf_{r↓0} H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x))/(ω r^n) ≥ β^{−n} and limsup_{r↓0} H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x))/(ω r^n) ≤ β^n.
 In particular H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) > 0 for all small r > 0.

6. Density of Γ for λ. By Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for the finite measure λ and the set Γ: for (λ.restrict Γ)-a.e. x, λ(Γ ∩ B_r(x))/λ(B_r(x)) → 1 as r ↓ 0. Since Γ and B_r(x) are closed, λ(Γ ∩ B_r(x)) = H^n(Γ ∩ B_r(x) ∩ A) = H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) (Measure.restrict_apply). Moreover λ.restrict Γ = H^n.restrict (Γ ∩ A) (Measure.restrict_restrict, Γ Borel); Γ ∩ A is H^n-null-measurable, so (λ.restrict Γ)-a.e. x lies in A_c, and (λ.restrict Γ)(X_c) ≤ H^n(X_c) = 0.

7. Combining. For (λ.restrict Γ)-a.e. x we therefore have x ∈ A_c ∖ X_c together with the convergence in 6. For small r, λ(B_r(x)) < ∞ and λ(Γ ∩ B_r(x)) = H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) > 0 (by 5), so λ(B_r(x))/(ω r^n) = [λ(B_r(x))/λ(Γ ∩ B_r(x))] · [H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x))/(ω r^n)], where the first factor tends to 1; by 5,
 β^{−n} ≤ liminf_{r↓0} densityRatio n λ x r ≤ limsup_{r↓0} densityRatio n λ x r ≤ β^n.

8. All of A. W_L := ⋃_{c ∈ C_L} c.2 is a countable union of closed sets, hence Borel, and A ⊆ W_L; so λ(ℝ^N ∖ W_L) = H^n((ℝ^N ∖ W_L) ∩ A) = 0 and λ = λ.restrict W_L. By ae_restrict_biUnion_iff / ae_restrict_iUnion_iff (C_L countable) and 7, the bounds of 7 with β = (1 + L²)^{1/2} hold for λ-a.e. x. (If C_L = ∅ then A = ∅, λ = 0, and everything is trivial.)

9. Apply 8 with L = 1/l for l = 1, 2, … and intersect the countably many full-measure sets (ae_all_iff): for λ-a.e. x and every l, (1 + l^{−2})^{−n/2} ≤ liminf_{r↓0} densityRatio n λ x r ≤ limsup_{r↓0} densityRatio n λ x r ≤ (1 + l^{−2})^{n/2}. Letting l → ∞ gives liminf = limsup = 1, hence densityRatio n λ x r → 1 as r ↓ 0 (tendsto_of_liminf_eq_limsup), i.e. HasDensity n λ x 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: n = 0: A is finite, ω_0 = 1, so the density of H^0⌞A is 1 at each point of A.
On a closed L-graph Γ over P: |p y − p z| ≤ |y − z| ≤ (1+L²)^{1/2}|p y − p z|; p injective with (1+L²)^{1/2}-Lipschitz inverse h.
Lipschitz image bounds: H^n(p(A_c) ∩ B_{r/β}(px)) ≤ H^n(A_c ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ β^n H^n(p(A_c) ∩ B_r(px)).
Lebesgue density theorem in the plane through an isometry ℝ^n → P.plane; the exceptional set pulls back to an H^n-null set via h.
Besicovitch density of the closed set Γ for λ = H^n⌞A converts H^n(A ∩ Γ ∩ B_r) into λ(B_r).
Countable union over C_L gives bounds (1+L²)^{∓n/2} λ-a.e.; L = 1/l → 0 gives density 1.

subproblem.title: μ-null sets of positive upper density are H^n-null (Ch. 1, 3.3 with outer regularity)
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^N be open, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^N with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and Z ⊆ U with μ(Z) = 0 and limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) > 0 for every x ∈ Z. Then H^n(Z) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (U Z : Set (Euclidean N)), IsOpen U → (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K ≠ ∞) → Z ⊆ U → μ Z = 0 → (∀ x ∈ Z, 0 < limsup (densityRatio n μ x) (𝓝[>] 0)) → μHE[n] Z = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step (3b) of the parent proof of Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2 (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.3 — if Θ^{*n}(μ, x) ≥ t on A₁ ⊆ A₂ then t H^n(A₁) ≤ μ(A₂) — combined with outer regularity). Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n; B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ; H^n := μHE[n].

0. Compact exhaustion. If U = ℝ^N let K_p := closedBall 0 p; otherwise K_p := {x : |x| ≤ p and infDist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) ≥ 1/p} (p ≥ 1). Each K_p is closed and bounded, hence compact; K_p ⊆ U (points of ℝ^N ∖ U have infDist 0); K_p ⊆ {x : |x| < p + 1, infDist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) > 1/(p + 1)} ⊆ interior K_{p+1} (the middle set is open); and ⋃_p K_p = U (for x ∈ U, infDist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) > 0 because ℝ^N ∖ U is closed and x ∉ ℝ^N ∖ U). Put W_p := interior K_{p+1}: open, K_p ⊆ W_p ⊆ U, μ(W_p) ≤ μ(K_{p+1}) < ∞.

1. Case n = 0. Let x ∈ Z. Choose r₀ > 0 with closedBall x r₀ ⊆ U; then μ(B_{r₀}(x)) < ∞ and ⋂_{ρ>0} B_ρ(x) = {x}, so by continuity from above μ(B_ρ(x)) → μ({x}) ≤ μ(Z) = 0 as ρ ↓ 0. As ω = unitBallVolume 0 ∈ (0, ∞) and ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^0 = 1, densityRatio 0 μ x ρ = μ(B_ρ(x))/ω → 0, so the limsup is 0, contradicting the hypothesis. Hence Z = ∅ and H^0(Z) = 0. From now on n ≥ 1.

2. Decomposition. For p, m ≥ 1 let Z_{p,m} := {x ∈ Z ∩ K_p : limsup_{ρ↓0} densityRatio n μ x ρ ≥ 1/m}. Every x ∈ Z lies in some K_p (Z ⊆ U), and its limsup is positive, hence ≥ 1/m for some m (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt). So Z = ⋃_{p,m} Z_{p,m}, and it suffices to show H^n(Z_{p,m}) = 0.

3. A small open neighbourhood. Fix p, m and ζ > 0. ν := μ.restrict W_p is a finite Borel measure on the metric space ℝ^N, hence outer regular (Mathlib Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure, MeasureTheory/Measure/Regular.lean:1072). ν(Z_{p,m}) ≤ μ(Z) = 0 < ζ, so outer regularity for arbitrary sets (Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt, which applies to any set; equivalently pass through the measurable hull toMeasurable ν Z_{p,m}) gives an open O' ⊇ Z_{p,m} with ν(O') < ζ. Let O := O' ∩ W_p: O is open, Z_{p,m} ⊆ O (as Z_{p,m} ⊆ K_p ⊆ W_p) and μ(O) = ν(O') < ζ (Measure.restrict_apply).

4. Density comparison. For x ∈ Z_{p,m}, O is a neighbourhood of x, so O ∩ B_ρ(x) = B_ρ(x) for small ρ > 0. Simon's upper density SimonGMT Chapter01.dimensionalUpperDensity μ.toOuterMeasure (n : ℝ) O x = limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(O ∩ B_ρ(x))/(realUnitBallVolume n · ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^n) (Chapter01/Densities.lean) therefore equals limsup_{ρ↓0} densityRatio n μ x ρ ≥ 1/m, because unitBallVolume n = volume(ball 0 1) = realUnitBallVolume n for n ≥ 1 (SimonGMT Chapter01.volume_euclidean_ball_eq with x = 0, r = 1, Chapter01/EuclideanHausdorffUpper.lean:71) and ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^(n:ℝ) = ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^n. By SimonGMT Chapter01.mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity (Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean:251; its hypothesis borel ℝ^N ≤ μ.toOuterMeasure.caratheodory holds because μ is a Borel measure) with A₁ := Z_{p,m}, A₂ := O and t := 1/m: (1/m) · simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n (Z_{p,m}) ≤ μ(O) < ζ.

5. Normalisation and conclusion. simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n = (simonHausdorffMeasureReal n).toOuterMeasure (SimonGMT Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure, Chapter01/Hausdorff.lean:445) and simonHausdorffMeasureReal (n : ℝ) = μHE[n] (SimonGMT Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, Chapter02/AreaLiteral.lean:42). Hence H^n(Z_{p,m}) ≤ m ζ for every ζ > 0, so H^n(Z_{p,m}) = 0, and H^n(Z) = 0 by 2. (The modules Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.DensityComparison, Chapter01.EuclideanHausdorffUpper and Chapter02.AreaLiteral must be imported; their axioms are propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Compact exhaustion K_p ⊆ interior K_{p+1} of U; W_p := interior K_{p+1} has finite μ-measure.
n = 0: positive limsup contradicts μ({x}) ≤ μ(Z) = 0, so Z = ∅.
Split Z into Z_{p,m} ⊆ K_p with upper density ≥ 1/m.
Outer regularity of the finite measure μ⌞W_p: open O ⊇ Z_{p,m} with μ(O) < ζ.

subproblem.title: Sets covered by countably many 1-graphs over n-planes are countably n-rectifiable
subproblem.statement: Let C ⊆ G(N,n) × 2^{ℝ^N} be countable such that for every c = (P, Γ) ∈ C, Γ is a 1-graph over P (|q_P(y − z)| ≤ |p_P(y − z)| for all y, z ∈ Γ, p_P = Grassmannian.project P, q_P = I − p_P), and let M ⊆ ⋃_{c ∈ C} c.2. Then M is countably n-rectifiable (Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n M, Simon Ch. 3, 1.1).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (C : Set (Grassmannian N n × Set (Euclidean N))), C.Countable → (∀ c ∈ C, ∀ y ∈ c.2, ∀ z ∈ c.2, ‖(y - z) - Grassmannian.project c.1 (y - z)‖ ≤ ‖Grassmannian.project c.1 (y - z)‖) → M ⊆ ⋃ c ∈ C, c.2 → Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n M

Source: Step 2 of the parent proof (Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 ⇐, p. 74: every piece lies in the rotated graph of a Lipschitz map, by the Lipschitz extension theorem Ch. 2, 1.2). Notation: for P ∈ G := Grassmannian N n, p := Grassmannian.project P; ℝ^n := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).

1. Linear algebra. projectionLinearMap P is symmetric and idempotent (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_isSymmetric, Grassmannian.project_project), so ⟨p v, v − p v⟩ = ⟨v, p v − p(p v)⟩ = 0 and |v|² = |p v|² + |v − p v|²; in particular |p v| ≤ |v|. Its range is P.plane, of dimension n (Grassmannian.finrank_plane).

2. One graph. Fix c = (P, Γ) ∈ C. For y, z ∈ Γ, by 1 and the hypothesis, |y − z|² = |p(y − z)|² + |(y − z) − p(y − z)|² ≤ 2|p y − p z|². Hence p is injective on Γ, and h := Function.invFunOn p Γ satisfies h(p y) = y for y ∈ Γ and |h a − h b| ≤ √2 |a − b| for a, b ∈ p(Γ) (LipschitzOnWith √2 h (p '' Γ)).

3. Parametrising the plane. Let e : ℝ^n ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] P.plane be a linear isometry equivalence (inverse coordinates of an orthonormal basis of P.plane, reindexed by Fin n via finrank P.plane = n) and ι := Subtype.val ∘ e : ℝ^n → ℝ^N, an isometry with range P.plane. Let S := ι⁻¹(p(Γ)) ⊆ ℝ^n and k := h ∘ ι. For a, b ∈ S, |k a − k b| ≤ √2 |ι a − ι b| = √2 |a − b|.

4. Extension (McShane). For each coordinate j ∈ Fin N the function k_j(a) := (k a) j is √2-Lipschitz on S (|u j − w j| ≤ |u − w| in EuclideanSpace), so by LipschitzOnWith.extend_real (Mathlib Topology/MetricSpace/Lipschitz.lean:308) there is a √2-Lipschitz g_j : ℝ^n → ℝ with g_j = k_j on S. Let F_c : ℝ^n → ℝ^N be the vector with coordinates g_j, F_c a := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j ↦ g_j a). Then |F_c a − F_c b|² = Σ_j |g_j a − g_j b|² ≤ 2N |a − b|², so F_c is Lipschitz (with constant √(2N)), and F_c = k on S. Each F_j is Lipschitz by 4, and M ⊆ ⋃_{c ∈ C} c.2 ⊆ ⋃_j range F_j by 5. This is exactly Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n M (∃ M₀ with μHE[n] M₀ = 0 and Lipschitz F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^N, j ∈ ℕ, with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j). (Equivalently: each c.2 ⊆ range F_c is countably rectifiable by Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_range and Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable.mono; conclude with Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_sUnion for the countable family {c.2 : c ∈ C} and .mono.) ∎

p_P is injective on Γ with √2-Lipschitz inverse h on p_P(Γ).
Compose with a linear isometry ℝ^n → P.plane and extend coordinatewise (McShane) to a Lipschitz F_c : ℝ^n → ℝ^N with Γ ⊆ range F_c.

subproblem.title: All tangent points lie on countably many closed L-graphs (net-of-planes step of Ch. 3, 1.6 ⇐)
subproblem.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N. Suppose that for every L ∈ (0,1] and every P ∈ G(N,n) there are closed sets Γ_0, Γ_1, … ⊆ ℝ^N, each an L-graph over P (|q_P(y − z)| ≤ L|p_P(y − z)| for y, z ∈ Γ_i, where p_P = Grassmannian.project P and q_P = I − p_P), such that every x with HasTangentPlane V x T θ and |p_T v − p_P v| ≤ (L/4)|v| for all v lies in some Γ_i (the conclusion of the sibling tangent_points_lipschitz_graph_cover for V). Then for every L ∈ (0,1] there is a countable set C of pairs (P, Γ) ∈ G(N,n) × 2^{ℝ^N}, each Γ closed and an L-graph over P, whose sets cover {x : ∃ T θ, HasTangentPlane V x T θ}.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the net-of-planes step in Steps 2 and 5 of the parent proof ("choose P_1, …, P_J ∈ G such that every T ∈ G satisfies ‖p_T − p_{P_j}‖ ≤ L/4 for some j"), which is the choice of the reference planes π_1, …, π_N in Simon's printed proof of Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 ⇐ (p. 73). A countable dense family of planes replaces the finite net; this suffices because the resulting cover is countable anyway. Notation: G := Grassmannian N n; p_S := Grassmannian.project S (the function of the linear map projectionLinearMap S); "Γ is an L-graph over P" means ‖(y − z) − p_P(y − z)‖ ≤ L‖p_P(y − z)‖ for all y, z ∈ Γ.

1. Fix L ∈ (0, 1] and put ε := L/4 > 0.

2. Continuity of S ↦ p_S. Let Φ : G → (ℝ^N →L[ℝ] ℝ^N) send S to projectionLinearMap S regarded as a continuous linear map (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap). Φ is continuous: S ↦ S.1 is the continuous inclusion of the subtype into the real N×N matrices, and M ↦ LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap ((LinearMap.toMatrix b b).symm M) (b the standard orthonormal basis) is a linear map between finite-dimensional spaces, hence continuous (LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional). Moreover Φ(S) v = p_S v. [Elementary alternative: |p_S v − p_{S'} v| ≤ (Σ_{i,j} (S_{ij} − S'_{ij})²)^{1/2} |v| by Cauchy–Schwarz in each coordinate.]

3. Countable net. G is a subspace of the second-countable metrizable space of real N×N matrices, hence second countable and separable; let D ⊆ G be countable and dense (TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense). For T ∈ G the set {S ∈ G : ‖Φ S − Φ T‖ < ε} is open by 2 and contains T, so it contains some P ∈ D. Then for every v ∈ ℝ^N, |p_T v − p_P v| = |(Φ T − Φ P) v| ≤ ‖Φ T − Φ P‖ |v| ≤ (L/4)|v|.

4. For each P ∈ D the hypothesis (applied with this L and P) provides Γ^P : ℕ → Set ℝ^N such that (a) every Γ^P_i is closed, (b) every Γ^P_i is an L-graph over P, and (c) every x with HasTangentPlane V x T θ and |p_T v − p_P v| ≤ (L/4)|v| for all v lies in some Γ^P_i. Fix such a choice for every P ∈ D (classical choice). Put C := {(P, Γ^P_i) : P ∈ D, i ∈ ℕ}, the image of the countable set D ×ˢ univ ⊆ G × ℕ under (P, i) ↦ (P, Γ^P_i); C is countable (Set.Countable.prod, Set.Countable.image).

5. For c = (P, Γ^P_i) ∈ C, c.2 = Γ^P_i is closed by (a) and an L-graph over c.1 = P by (b).

6. Covering. Let x satisfy HasTangentPlane V x T θ. By 3 there is P ∈ D with |p_T v − p_P v| ≤ (L/4)|v| for all v, and by (c) there is i with x ∈ Γ^P_i; thus x ∈ ⋃_{c ∈ C} c.2, witnessed by c = (P, Γ^P_i) ∈ C. (If G = ∅, i.e. n > N, then D = C = ∅ and there are no tangent points, so the statement holds as well.) ∎

A countable dense D ⊆ G yields, for every T, some P ∈ D with |p_T v − p_P v| ≤ (L/4)|v|.
Apply the per-plane cover hypothesis to every P ∈ D.
C := {(P, Γ^P_i)} is countable; its sets are closed L-graphs and cover all tangent points.

subproblem.title: H^n-null sets on which μ has finite density are μ-null
subproblem.statement: Let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N and Z ⊆ ℝ^N with H^n(Z) = 0 such that at every x ∈ Z the n-density of μ exists and is finite (HasDensity n μ x θ for some θ ∈ [0, ∞)). Then μ(Z) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (Z : Set (Euclidean N)), μHE[n] Z = 0 → (∀ x ∈ Z, ∃ θ : ℝ≥0∞, θ ≠ ∞ ∧ HasDensity n μ x θ) → μ Z = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step (3a) of the parent proof of Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2 (the covering comparison of Ch. 1, 3.2(2): if Θ^{*n}(μ, x) ≤ t on A then μ(A) ≤ 2^n t H^n(A)). Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞); B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ; μH[n] is Mathlib's (unnormalised) n-dimensional Hausdorff measure and H^n := μHE[n] = c_n · μH[n] with c_n ∈ (0, ∞) (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def); diam is the extended diameter, and ENNReal powers satisfy 0^0 = 1.

1. Decomposition. For k ∈ ℕ and j ≥ 1 let Z_{k,j} := {x ∈ Z : μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ (k + 1) ω ρ^n for all ρ ∈ (0, 1/j]}. Then Z = ⋃_{k,j} Z_{k,j}: if x ∈ Z and HasDensity n μ x θ with θ < ∞, choose k ∈ ℕ with θ < k + 1; since densityRatio n μ x ρ → θ as ρ ↓ 0, there is j ≥ 1 with densityRatio n μ x ρ < k + 1 for all ρ ∈ (0, 1/j], and as ω · ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^n ∈ (0, ∞) for ρ > 0 this gives μ(B_ρ(x)) < (k + 1) ω ρ^n. By countable subadditivity it suffices to show μ(Z_{k,j}) = 0 for all k, j.

2. Fix k, j, put δ := 1/j and c := (k + 1) ω < ∞. Since Z_{k,j} ⊆ Z, H^n(Z_{k,j}) = 0, hence μH[n](Z_{k,j}) = 0 (c_n ≠ 0).

3. Covers. By Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply (MeasureTheory/Measure/Hausdorff.lean:546), μH[n](Z_{k,j}) = ⨆_{r>0} ⨅ {Σ_i ⨆_{t_i ≠ ∅} diam(t_i)^n : Z_{k,j} ⊆ ⋃_i t_i, diam t_i ≤ r ∀ i}. As this is 0, for r := ENNReal.ofReal δ and every ζ > 0 the inner infimum is < ζ, so there is a sequence (t_i)_{i∈ℕ} with Z_{k,j} ⊆ ⋃_i t_i, diam t_i ≤ δ for all i, and Σ_{i : t_i ≠ ∅} diam(t_i)^n < ζ.

4. One covering set. Let i be such that t_i ∩ Z_{k,j} ≠ ∅; pick x_i ∈ t_i ∩ Z_{k,j} and put d_i := diam t_i ∈ [0, δ]. Then t_i ⊆ B_{d_i}(x_i). Claim: μ(t_i ∩ Z_{k,j}) ≤ c · d_i^n.
 – If d_i > 0: μ(t_i ∩ Z_{k,j}) ≤ μ(B_{d_i}(x_i)) ≤ c d_i^n, because d_i ∈ (0, δ] and x_i ∈ Z_{k,j}.
 – If d_i = 0: t_i = {x_i} and μ({x_i}) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x_i)) ≤ c ρ^n for every ρ ∈ (0, δ]. For n ≥ 1, letting ρ ↓ 0 gives μ({x_i}) = 0 = c · 0^n; for n = 0 it gives μ({x_i}) ≤ c = c · 0^0.

5. Summation. Sets t_i not meeting Z_{k,j} contribute nothing, so by countable subadditivity μ(Z_{k,j}) ≤ Σ_i μ(t_i ∩ Z_{k,j}) ≤ c Σ_{i : t_i ≠ ∅} diam(t_i)^n ≤ c ζ. Since ζ > 0 is arbitrary and c < ∞, μ(Z_{k,j}) = 0. By 1, μ(Z) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Z is the countable union of Z_{k,j} = {μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ (k+1)ω_nρ^n for 0 < ρ ≤ 1/j} by finiteness of the density.
H^n(Z_{k,j}) = 0 gives covers by sets of diameter ≤ 1/j with Σ diam^n < ζ (hausdorffMeasure_apply).
Each covering set meeting Z_{k,j} lies in a ball B_{d_i}(x_i) with μ ≤ (k+1)ω_n d_i^n (degenerate d_i = 0 handled separately).
μ(Z_{k,j}) ≤ (k+1)ω_n ζ for every ζ > 0.

audit.reason: Finite densities give the stated countable decomposition with uniform ball bounds. Hausdorff-null covers and summation force zero measure, with zero-diameter covering sets handled for both zero and positive dimensions. No unstated regularity or sigma-finiteness is needed.

subproblem.title: The carrier of positive densities is H^n-measurable (printed 'M is H^n-measurable')
subproblem.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N, μ := μ_V, M ⊆ U with μ(ℝ^N ∖ M) = 0, and θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with θ(x) > 0 and Θ^n(μ, x) = θ(x) (HasDensity n μ x (ENNReal.ofReal θ(x))) for every x ∈ M. Then M is H^n-null-measurable.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ), M ⊆ U → V.weight Mᶜ = 0 → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x ∧ HasDensity n V.weight x (ENNReal.ofReal (θ x))) → NullMeasurableSet M μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4 of the parent proof of Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2 (the printed claim "M is H^n-measurable", supplied here because Ch. 3, 1.9 presupposes it). Notation: μ := V.weight; ω := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞); B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ; H^n := μHE[n].

0. U is open (V.isOpen_domain) and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact).

1. Uniform pieces. For m, k ≥ 1 let F_{m,k} := {x ∈ M : θ(x) ≥ 1/m and μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ (2m)^{−1} ω ρ^n for all ρ ∈ (0, 1/k]}. Then M = ⋃_{m,k} F_{m,k}: for x ∈ M choose m with θ(x) ≥ 1/m; since densityRatio n μ x ρ → ENNReal.ofReal θ(x) > (2m)^{−1} as ρ ↓ 0, there is k with densityRatio n μ x ρ > (2m)^{−1} for ρ ∈ (0, 1/k], i.e. μ(B_ρ(x)) > (2m)^{−1} ω ρ^n.

2. Countably many balls. Let D₀ ⊆ ℝ^N be countable and dense and let 𝓑 be the countable family of closed balls B_r(x₀) with x₀ ∈ D₀, r ∈ ℚ, r > 0 and closedBall x₀ (2r) ⊆ U. 𝓑 covers U: for x ∈ U pick a rational r > 0 with closedBall x (4r) ⊆ U and x₀ ∈ D₀ with |x − x₀| < r; then x ∈ B_r(x₀) and closedBall x₀ (2r) ⊆ closedBall x (3r) ⊆ U.

3. For m, k ≥ 1 and B ∈ 𝓑 let E := F_{m,k} ∩ B and Ē := closure E. Then Ē ⊆ B (B is closed), so Ē is compact and contained in U.

4. Lower density on the closure. Let y ∈ Ē and ρ ∈ (0, 1/k]. Choose x_i ∈ E with x_i → y. For all large i, |x_i − y| < ρ, ρ_i := ρ − |x_i − y| ∈ (0, 1/k] and B_{ρ_i}(x_i) ⊆ B_ρ(y), so μ(B_ρ(y)) ≥ μ(B_{ρ_i}(x_i)) ≥ (2m)^{−1} ω ρ_i^n; letting i → ∞, μ(B_ρ(y)) ≥ (2m)^{−1} ω ρ^n. Hence densityRatio n μ y ρ ≥ (2m)^{−1} for all ρ ∈ (0, 1/k], and limsup_{ρ↓0} densityRatio n μ y ρ ≥ (2m)^{−1} > 0.

5. The defect is H^n-null. Z := Ē ∖ M satisfies Z ⊆ Ē ⊆ U, μ(Z) ≤ μ(ℝ^N ∖ M) = 0, and the density condition of 4 at each of its points. By frt_hausdorff_null_of_weight_null (with this μ, U and Z), H^n(Ē ∖ M) = 0.

6. M ∩ Ē = Ē ∖ (Ē ∖ M) is the difference of a closed (hence Borel) set and an H^n-null set, so it is H^n-null-measurable (MeasurableSet.nullMeasurableSet, NullMeasurableSet.diff with NullMeasurableSet.of_null).

7. M = ⋃_{m,k ≥ 1, B ∈ 𝓑} (M ∩ Ē_{m,k,B}). "⊇" is clear. "⊆": a point x ∈ M lies in some F_{m,k} (1) and, since M ⊆ U, in some B ∈ 𝓑 (2); then x ∈ E ⊆ Ē. A countable union of H^n-null-measurable sets is H^n-null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.iUnion), so M is H^n-null-measurable. ∎
proof_key_steps: M = ⋃ F_{m,k} with θ ≥ 1/m and the uniform lower bound μ_V(B_ρ) ≥ (2m)^{-1}ω_nρ^n for ρ ≤ 1/k.
Intersect with countably many closed balls compactly inside U.
The lower bound passes to the closure Ē (shrinking balls).
Ē ∖ M is μ_V-null with positive upper density, hence H^n-null by frt_hausdorff_null_of_weight_null.
M is a countable union of the null-measurable sets Ē ∖ (Ē ∖ M).

audit.reason: Uniform positive lower-density pieces cover the carrier, and their bounds pass to compact closures. The declared comparison dependency makes each closure defect Hausdorff-null. Countable union then proves precisely null-measurability, without presupposing carrier measurability.

subproblem.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N, x ∈ ℝ^N, T ∈ G(N,n), θ ∈ ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ. Then the n-dimensional density of μ_V at x exists and equals θ: μ_V(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) → θ as ρ ↓ 0, i.e. HasDensity n V.weight x (ENNReal.ofReal θ) (closed balls B_ρ(x), ω_n = unitBallVolume n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ → HasDensity n V.weight x (ENNReal.ofReal θ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step (0c) of the parent proof of Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2 (cf. Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)). Notation: μ := V.weight; ω := unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : ℝ^n) 1) where ℝ^n := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ; H^n := μHE[n].

1. By HasTangentPlane, x ∈ U and θ > 0. U is open (V.isOpen_domain), so there is r₀ > 0 with closedBall x r₀ ⊆ U; for 0 < t ≤ r₀ the ball B_t(x) is compact and contained in U, hence μ(B_t(x)) < ∞ (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact).

2. ω ∈ (0, ∞): the open unit ball of ℝ^n is a nonempty bounded open set and volume is an additive Haar measure (measure_ball_pos, measure_ball_lt_top).

3. Plane balls: H^n(T.plane ∩ B_κ(0)) = ω κ^n for κ > 0. Indeed finrank T.plane = n (Grassmannian.finrank_plane), so there is a linear isometry equivalence e : ℝ^n ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] T.plane (coordinates of an orthonormal basis of T.plane indexed by Fin n); ι := Subtype.val ∘ e : ℝ^n → ℝ^N is an isometry with range T.plane, and ι(closedBall 0 κ) = T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 κ (ι is linear, norm-preserving and onto T.plane). By Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume (Mathlib Geometry/Euclidean/Volume/Measure.lean:131,187), H^n(T.plane ∩ B_κ(0)) = volume(closedBall (0 : ℝ^n) κ) = ENNReal.ofReal(κ^n) · ω (Measure.addHaar_closedBall, finrank ℝ^n = n). (For n = 0 this reads H^0({0}) = 1 = ω.) In particular H^n⌞T.plane is finite on bounded sets, so every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) is H^n⌞T.plane-integrable.

4. Cutoffs: for 0 < a < b put χ_{a,b}(y) := max(0, min(1, (b − |y|)/(b − a))). It is continuous, 0 ≤ χ_{a,b} ≤ 1, χ_{a,b} = 1 on B_a(0) and χ_{a,b} = 0 outside ball 0 b; hence tsupport χ_{a,b} ⊆ B_b(0) is compact and χ_{a,b} ∈ C_c(ℝ^N).

5. Lower bound. Let κ ∈ (0, 1) and g := χ_{κ,1}. For 0 < t ≤ r₀ and all z, 0 ≤ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) ≤ 1_{B_t(x)}(z). The function z ↦ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) is continuous, bounded and vanishes outside B_t(x), which has finite μ-measure, so it is μ-integrable and ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ ≤ μ(B_t(x)).toReal. By frt_weight_blowup_tendsto, t⁻¹ ^ n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ → θ ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n ≥ θ (H^n(T.plane ∩ B_κ(0))).toReal = θ ω.toReal κ^n (g ≥ 1 on B_κ(0), g ≥ 0, θ > 0). Hence liminf_{t↓0} t^{−n} μ(B_t(x)).toReal ≥ θ ω.toReal κ^n.

6. Upper bound. Let κ > 1 and g := χ_{1,κ}. For 0 < t ≤ r₀/κ, 1_{B_t(x)}(z) ≤ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) ≤ 1_{B_{κt}(x)}(z) and μ(B_{κt}(x)) < ∞, so μ(B_t(x)).toReal ≤ ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ, and by frt_weight_blowup_tendsto, t⁻¹ ^ n times the right-hand side tends to θ ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n ≤ θ (H^n(T.plane ∩ B_κ(0))).toReal = θ ω.toReal κ^n (g ≤ 1_{B_κ(0)}). Hence limsup_{t↓0} t^{−n} μ(B_t(x)).toReal ≤ θ ω.toReal κ^n.

7. Letting κ ↑ 1 in 5 and κ ↓ 1 in 6 gives t^{−n} μ(B_t(x)).toReal → θ ω.toReal as t ↓ 0.

8. For 0 < t ≤ r₀ the quantities μ(B_t(x)), ω, ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n are finite and the last two are positive, so densityRatio n μ x t = μ(B_t(x)) / (ω · ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n) = ENNReal.ofReal(t^{−n} μ(B_t(x)).toReal / ω.toReal). By 7 and continuity of ENNReal.ofReal, densityRatio n μ x t → ENNReal.ofReal(θ ω.toReal / ω.toReal) = ENNReal.ofReal θ as t ↓ 0, which is HasDensity n V.weight x (ENNReal.ofReal θ). ∎

subproblem.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N, M ⊆ ℝ^N H^n-null-measurable, θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with θ > 0 on M, θ H^n-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U, and μ_V(B) = ∫_{B ∩ M} θ dH^n for every Borel B. If HasTangentPlane V x T (θ(x)), then for every S ∈ G(N,n): M has approximate tangent space S.plane at x with respect to θ in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7 (Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane) if and only if S = T.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n), NullMeasurableSet M μHE[n] → (∀ y ∈ M, 0 < θ y) → (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) μHE[n]) → (∀ B : Set (Euclidean N), MeasurableSet B → V.weight B = ∫⁻ y in B ∩ M, ENNReal.ofReal (θ y) ∂μHE[n]) → HasTangentPlane V x T (θ x) → ∀ S : Grassmannian N n, Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane ↔ S = T
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 7 of the parent proof of Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2 (the printed "V has approximate tangent space T_x with multiplicity θ(x) in the sense of 1.7 of Ch. 3"). Notation: μ := V.weight; H^n := μHE[n]; blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹ • (y − x) (SimonGMT Chapter03/Rectifiable.lean); Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P means finrank P = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' M} f(y) θ(x + r • y) dH^n(y) → θ(x) ∫_P f dH^n as r ↓ 0.

1. From HasTangentPlane V x T (θ x): x ∈ U and θ(x) > 0. Also finrank T.plane = n (Grassmannian.finrank_plane).

2. μ as a weighted Hausdorff measure on compact pieces. Let K' ⊆ U be compact and h : ℝ^N → ℝ bounded, Borel and zero outside K'. Then ∫ h dμ = ∫_{M ∩ K'} h θ dH^n, both integrands being integrable. Proof: ν := μ.restrict K' is finite (μ(K') < ∞ by the hypothesis with B := K' and integrability on M ∩ K', or by Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact); ν' := (H^n.restrict (M ∩ K')).withDensity (ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ). For Borel B, ν(B) = μ(B ∩ K') = ∫⁻_{B ∩ K' ∩ M} ENNReal.ofReal θ dH^n = ν'(B) (hypothesis applied to the Borel set B ∩ K'; withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict), so ν = ν' (Measure.ext). θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n.restrict (M ∩ K') (from IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K')), and θ = (ENNReal.ofReal (θ ·)).toReal holds H^n.restrict (M ∩ K')-a.e. because M ∩ K' is null-measurable (ae_restrict_mem₀) and θ > 0 on M. Hence ∫ h dν' = ∫ h θ d(H^n.restrict (M ∩ K')) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ or integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul₀), where |h θ| ≤ (sup |h|) |θ| is integrable. Since h = 0 off K', ∫ h dμ = ∫ h dν.

3. Homothety change of variables. Fix r > 0 and let φ := blowUpMap x r, a homeomorphism of ℝ^N (hence a measurable equivalence) with inverse y ↦ x + r • y. For Borel S, (H^n.map φ)(S) = H^n(φ⁻¹ S) = H^n(x + r • S) = r^n H^n(S) (translation is an isometry, Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, and Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀; or directly euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_preimage, Mathlib Geometry/Euclidean/Volume/Measure.lean:152–172), so H^n.map φ = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H^n. By MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map and φ⁻¹(φ '' M) = M, (H^n.restrict M).map φ = (H^n.map φ).restrict (φ '' M) = ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) • H^n.restrict (φ '' M). Consequently, for every function F : ℝ^N → ℝ, ∫_{φ '' M} F dH^n = r⁻¹ ^ n ∫_M F(φ z) dH^n(z) (integral_smul_measure and MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).

4. The blow-up integrals. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), choose R ≥ 1 with tsupport f ⊆ closedBall 0 R, and r₀ > 0 with closedBall x (r₀ R) ⊆ U (U open, x ∈ U). For 0 < r ≤ r₀ apply 3 with F(y) := f(y) θ(x + r • y); then F(φ z) = f(r⁻¹ • (z − x)) θ(z), and with K' := closedBall x (r R) ⊆ U and h(z) := f(r⁻¹ • (z − x)) (continuous, bounded, zero outside K'), step 2 gives
 ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' M} f(y) θ(x + r • y) dH^n(y) = r⁻¹ ^ n ∫_M f(r⁻¹ • (z − x)) θ(z) dH^n(z) = r⁻¹ ^ n ∫ f(r⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ(z)
 (the middle integral equals ∫_{M ∩ K'} h θ dH^n because its integrand vanishes off K').

5. Limit. By frt_weight_blowup_tendsto (applied to the tangent plane T with multiplicity θ(x) and g := f), r⁻¹ ^ n ∫ f(r⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ(z) → θ(x) ∫_{T.plane} f dH^n as r ↓ 0. The left-hand side of 4 agrees with it on (0, r₀] ∈ 𝓝[>] 0, so it has the same limit. Together with finrank T.plane = n this proves Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T.plane.

6. The equivalence. If S = T, the approximate tangent property holds by 5. Conversely, if Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane, then by Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique (θ(x) ≠ 0) and 5, S.plane = T.plane, hence S = T because a point of G is determined by its plane (SimonGMT Grassmannian.eq_of_plane_eq, Chapter08/ConstancyTangent.lean:33, after importing Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.ConstancyTangent; directly: the symmetric idempotent matrix S.1 is the matrix of the orthogonal projection onto S.plane). ∎

Homothety change of variables: ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' M} F dH^n = r^{-n} ∫_M F(blowUpMap x r z) dH^n(z).
Hence the Ch. 3 1.7 blow-up integral equals r^{-n} ∫ f(r^{-1}(z − x)) dμ_V for small r, which tends to θ(x)∫_{T.plane} f dH^n by frt_weight_blowup_tendsto.

subproblem.title: Uniqueness of tangent plane and multiplicity in Def. 1.1
subproblem.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N and x ∈ ℝ^N. If HasTangentPlane V x T θ and HasTangentPlane V x T' θ', then T' = T and θ' = θ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (T T' : Grassmannian N n) (θ θ' : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ → HasTangentPlane V x T' θ' → T' = T ∧ θ' = θ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step (0d) of the parent proof of Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2 (limits of Radon measures are unique; cf. Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1)). Notation: μ := V.weight, H^n := μHE[n].

1. Multiplicity. By frt_tangent_plane_hasDensity, HasDensity n μ x (ENNReal.ofReal θ) and HasDensity n μ x (ENNReal.ofReal θ'), i.e. the function densityRatio n μ x tends to both values along 𝓝[>] 0, a non-trivial filter. By tendsto_nhds_unique, ENNReal.ofReal θ = ENNReal.ofReal θ'. Since θ > 0 and θ' > 0 (second clause of HasTangentPlane), θ = θ' (ENNReal.ofReal_eq_ofReal_iff).

2. Plane measures have equal integrals. Let g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N). By frt_weight_blowup_tendsto applied to (T, θ) and to (T', θ'), the same function t ↦ t⁻¹ ^ n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ(z) tends along 𝓝[>] 0 both to θ ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n and to θ' ∫_{T'.plane} g dH^n. By uniqueness of limits and θ = θ' ≠ 0, ∫ g d(H^n.restrict T.plane) = ∫ g d(H^n.restrict T'.plane).

3. Equality of measures. finrank T.plane = finrank T'.plane = n (Grassmannian.finrank_plane), so both H^n.restrict T.plane and H^n.restrict T'.plane are regular measures (SimonGMT Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule, Chapter03/Rectifiable.lean). By Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported (Mathlib MeasureTheory/Integral/RieszMarkovKakutani/Real.lean:412) and 2, H^n.restrict T.plane = H^n.restrict T'.plane.

4. Equality of planes. By SimonGMT Chapter03.support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule (the support of H^n⌞P is P for every n-dimensional subspace P), taking supports in 3 gives (T.plane : Set ℝ^N) = T'.plane, hence T.plane = T'.plane as submodules (SetLike.ext').

5. Equality of points of G. For S ∈ G the linear map p_S := projectionLinearMap S is symmetric and idempotent (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_isSymmetric, Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_comp_self) with range S.plane; for every v, p_S v ∈ S.plane and v − p_S v ⊥ S.plane (⟨v − p_S v, p_S w⟩ = ⟨p_S v − p_S(p_S v), w⟩ = 0), so p_S is the orthogonal projection onto S.plane. Therefore T.plane = T'.plane forces p_T = p_{T'}; since LinearMap.toMatrix is injective, the matrices T.1 and T'.1 coincide, i.e. T = T' in the subtype G. (This is SimonGMT Grassmannian.eq_of_plane_eq, Chapter08/ConstancyTangent.lean:33, usable after adding the import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.ConstancyTangent.) With 1, T' = T ∧ θ' = θ. ∎
proof_key_steps: θ = θ' by uniqueness of the density limit (frt_tangent_plane_hasDensity).
Equal C_c integrals against H^n⌞T.plane and H^n⌞T'.plane (frt_weight_blowup_tendsto, θ = θ' > 0).
Regular measures with equal C_c integrals are equal.
Supports give T.plane = T'.plane.
A projection matrix is determined by its plane, so T = T'.

subproblem.title: μ_V = θ H^n ⌞ M and local H^n-integrability of θ (Besicovitch differentiation and Radon–Nikodym)
subproblem.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N, μ := μ_V, M ⊆ U with μ(ℝ^N ∖ M) = 0, and θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with θ(x) > 0 and HasDensity n μ x (ENNReal.ofReal θ(x)) for every x ∈ M. Suppose that for every L ∈ (0,1], M is covered by a countable family of closed L-graphs over n-planes ((P, Γ) ∈ C_L, Γ closed, |q_P(y − z)| ≤ L|p_P(y − z)| on Γ). Then (a) θ is H^n-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U, and (b) μ(B) = ∫_{B ∩ M} θ dH^n (as the lintegral of ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ) for every μ-null-measurable B ⊆ ℝ^N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ), M ⊆ U → V.weight Mᶜ = 0 → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x ∧ HasDensity n V.weight x (ENNReal.ofReal (θ x))) → (∀ L : ℝ, 0 < L → L ≤ 1 → ∃ C : Set (Grassmannian N n × Set (Euclidean N)), C.Countable ∧ (∀ c ∈ C, IsClosed c.2 ∧ ∀ y ∈ c.2, ∀ z ∈ c.2, ‖(y - z) - Grassmannian.project c.1 (y - z)‖ ≤ L * ‖Grassmannian.project c.1 (y - z)‖) ∧ M ⊆ ⋃ c ∈ C, c.2) → (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) μHE[n]) ∧ ∀ B : Set (Euclidean N), NullMeasurableSet B V.weight → V.weight B = ∫⁻ x in B ∩ M, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6 of the parent proof of Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2 (the printed "μ_V = H^n ⌞ θ in U", obtained from the Besicovitch differentiation theorem and the Radon–Nikodym theorem, Ch. 1, 3.23–3.24), together with the parts of Steps 3 and (0f) it needs; the case n = 0 is the corresponding part of Step 1. Notation: μ := V.weight; ω := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞) (ω = 1 if n = 0, Mathlib volume_euclideanSpace_eq_dirac); B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ; H^n := μHE[n]; K_p (p ≥ 1) a compact exhaustion of U: K_p := closedBall 0 p if U = ℝ^N, and otherwise K_p := {x : |x| ≤ p and infDist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) ≥ 1/p}; each K_p is closed and bounded, hence compact; K_p ⊆ U (points of ℝ^N ∖ U have infDist 0); K_p ⊆ {x : |x| < p + 1, infDist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) > 1/(p + 1)} ⊆ interior K_{p+1} (the middle set is open); K_p ⊆ K_{p+1}; and ⋃_p K_p = U (for x ∈ U, infDist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) > 0 since ℝ^N ∖ U is closed and does not contain x).

0. Standing facts. U is open (V.isOpen_domain); μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact); μ is σ-finite (Varifold.weight.instSigmaFinite). By frt_carrier_nullMeasurable, M is H^n-null-measurable.

1. Borel representative of θ. For r > 0, x ↦ μ(B_r(x)) is Borel (Mathlib measurable_measure_prodMk_left for the s-finite measure μ and the closed, hence Borel, set {(x, y) : dist y x ≤ r} ⊆ ℝ^N × ℝ^N, whose section at x is closedBall x r; SimonGMT Chapter01.measurable_closedBall_mass_of_sFinite states the same fact but under a local Borel instance, so it does not apply verbatim), hence so is x ↦ densityRatio n μ x r (division by a constant), and Θ̂(x) := liminf_{k→∞} densityRatio n μ x (1/(k + 1)) is a Borel function ℝ^N → [0, ∞] (Measurable.liminf). For x ∈ M, densityRatio n μ x (1/(k + 1)) → ENNReal.ofReal θ(x) (HasDensity composed with 1/(k + 1) → 0⁺), so Θ̂(x) = ENNReal.ofReal θ(x) and θ(x) = (Θ̂ x).toReal. Consequently, on every H^n-null-measurable subset of M, θ and ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ agree everywhere with Borel functions, so they are a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to such a set.

2. μ-null subsets of M are H^n-null. If Z ⊆ M and μ(Z) = 0, then for x ∈ Z, limsup_{ρ↓0} densityRatio n μ x ρ = ENNReal.ofReal θ(x) > 0 (Tendsto.limsup_eq), so frt_hausdorff_null_of_weight_null (with this μ and U) gives H^n(Z) = 0.

3. Pieces. For p ≥ 1 put M_p := {x ∈ M : θ(x) ≥ 1/p} ∩ K_p = M ∩ {x : (Θ̂ x).toReal ≥ 1/p} ∩ K_p (by 1); it is H^n-null-measurable (null-measurable ∩ Borel ∩ closed). M_p ⊆ M_{p+1}, and ⋃_p M_p = M because θ > 0 on M, M ⊆ U = ⋃_p K_p and the K_p increase.

4. H^n(M_p) < ∞.
 – n ≥ 1: let W := interior K_{p+1}, an open set with M_p ⊆ K_p ⊆ W and μ(W) ≤ μ(K_{p+1}) < ∞. For x ∈ M_p, W is a neighbourhood of x, so W ∩ B_ρ(x) = B_ρ(x) for small ρ > 0. Simon's upper density SimonGMT Chapter01.dimensionalUpperDensity μ.toOuterMeasure (n : ℝ) W x = limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(W ∩ B_ρ(x))/(realUnitBallVolume n · ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^(n : ℝ)) (Chapter01/Densities.lean) therefore equals limsup_{ρ↓0} densityRatio n μ x ρ = ENNReal.ofReal θ(x) ≥ 1/p, because unitBallVolume n = volume(ball 0 1) = realUnitBallVolume n for n ≥ 1 (SimonGMT Chapter01.volume_euclidean_ball_eq with x = 0, r = 1, Chapter01/EuclideanHausdorffUpper.lean:71) and ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^(n : ℝ) = ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^n. SimonGMT Chapter01.mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity (Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean:251; its hypothesis borel ℝ^N ≤ μ.toOuterMeasure.caratheodory holds as μ is a Borel measure) with A₁ := M_p, A₂ := W, t := 1/p gives (1/p) · simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n (M_p) ≤ μ(W) < ∞; and simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n = (simonHausdorffMeasureReal n).toOuterMeasure (Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure) with simonHausdorffMeasureReal (n : ℝ) = μHE[n] (Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, Chapter02/AreaLiteral.lean:42), so H^n(M_p) ≤ p μ(W) < ∞. (Import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.DensityComparison, Chapter01.EuclideanHausdorffUpper and Chapter02.AreaLiteral.)
 – n = 0: for x ∈ M, μ(B_ρ(x)) → μ({x}) as ρ ↓ 0 (continuity from above; μ(B_ρ(x)) < ∞ for small ρ since x ∈ U), while densityRatio 0 μ x ρ = μ(B_ρ(x)) → θ(x) (ω = 1); so μ({x}) = θ(x). Thus M_p ⊆ K_p consists of atoms of mass ≥ 1/p, so M_p is finite with #M_p ≤ p μ(K_p) < ∞, and H^0(M_p) = #M_p < ∞ (μHE[0] = μH[0] and μH[0]{a} = 1).
 In both cases λ_p := H^n.restrict M_p is a finite Borel measure.

5. Density one (α). M_p ⊆ M, so for every L ∈ (0, 1] the countable family of closed L-graphs covering M also covers M_p. With 3 and 4, frt_hausdorff_density_one_of_flat_covers (A := M_p) gives: for λ_p-a.e. x, λ_p(B_r(x))/(ω r^n) → 1 as r ↓ 0.

6. ρ_p := μ.restrict M_p is a finite measure (ρ_p(ℝ^N) = μ(M_p) ≤ μ(K_p) < ∞), and ρ_p ≪ λ_p: if B is Borel with λ_p(B) = H^n(B ∩ M_p) = 0, then every point of B ∩ M_p ⊆ M has the finite density ENNReal.ofReal θ(x) ≠ ∞, so μ(B ∩ M_p) = 0 by frt_weight_null_of_hausdorff_null, i.e. ρ_p(B) = 0.

7. Radon–Nikodym. By Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv (Covering/Besicovitch.lean:1078) for the finite measures ρ_p and λ_p, for λ_p-a.e. x: ρ_p(B_r(x))/λ_p(B_r(x)) → (ρ_p.rnDeriv λ_p)(x) as r ↓ 0; and ρ_p = λ_p.withDensity (ρ_p.rnDeriv λ_p) by Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_eq (Decomposition/RadonNikodym.lean:60), since ρ_p ≪ λ_p.

8. Identification of the derivative. Let W := interior K_{p+1}. By Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div (Covering/Besicovitch.lean:1105) for the finite measure μ.restrict W and the set M_p: for ((μ.restrict W).restrict M_p)-a.e. x, (μ.restrict W)(M_p ∩ B_r(x))/(μ.restrict W)(B_r(x)) → 1. For x ∈ M_p ⊆ K_p ⊆ W and small r, B_r(x) ⊆ W, so this says (β): μ(M_p ∩ B_r(x))/μ(B_r(x)) → 1. The a.e. statement provides a Borel set E with ((μ.restrict W).restrict M_p)(E) = 0 containing every point at which (β) fails; since restricting to the Borel set E gives μ(E ∩ M_p ∩ W) = 0 (no measurability of M_p needed), the set E_β := {x ∈ M_p : (β) fails at x} ⊆ E ∩ M_p ∩ W is μ-null; as E_β ⊆ M, step 2 gives H^n(E_β) = 0 and hence λ_p(E_β) = 0. Also (γ): μ(B_r(x))/(ω r^n) → θ(x) ∈ (0, ∞) for every x ∈ M (hypothesis). Since M_p is H^n-null-measurable, λ_p-a.e. x lies in M_p (ae_restrict_mem₀). So for λ_p-a.e. x we have x ∈ M_p ∖ E_β, (α), (β), (γ) and the convergence of 7. At such x, for small r all of μ(B_r(x)), μ(M_p ∩ B_r(x)), λ_p(B_r(x)) are finite and positive, ρ_p(B_r(x)) = μ(B_r(x) ∩ M_p) (Measure.restrict_apply), and
 ρ_p(B_r(x))/λ_p(B_r(x)) = [μ(M_p ∩ B_r(x))/μ(B_r(x))] · [μ(B_r(x))/(ω r^n)] / [λ_p(B_r(x))/(ω r^n)] → 1 · ENNReal.ofReal θ(x) / 1.
 By uniqueness of limits, ρ_p.rnDeriv λ_p = ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ λ_p-a.e., so ρ_p = λ_p.withDensity (ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ) (withDensity_congr_ae). Evaluating on a Borel set B (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict): μ(B ∩ M_p) = ∫⁻_{B} ENNReal.ofReal θ dλ_p = ∫⁻_{B ∩ M_p} ENNReal.ofReal θ dH^n.

9. Borel sets. Let B be Borel. The sets B ∩ M_p increase to B ∩ M, so μ(B ∩ M) = sup_p μ(B ∩ M_p) (Monotone.measure_iUnion, which needs no measurability), and ∫⁻_{B ∩ M} ENNReal.ofReal θ dH^n = sup_p ∫⁻_{B ∩ M_p} ENNReal.ofReal θ dH^n (write the integrals as lintegrals of the indicators (B ∩ M_p).indicator (ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ), which by 1 and 3 coincide with indicators of null-measurable sets times the Borel function ENNReal.ofReal ∘ (Θ̂ ·).toReal and hence are H^n-a.e.-measurable, increase in p and converge pointwise to (B ∩ M).indicator (ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ); apply the monotone convergence theorem lintegral_iSup'). By 8, μ(B ∩ M) = ∫⁻_{B ∩ M} ENNReal.ofReal θ dH^n, and μ(B) = μ(B ∩ M) because μ(B ∖ M) ≤ μ(ℝ^N ∖ M) = 0.

10. Null-measurable sets (b). Let B be μ-null-measurable and choose a Borel B₀ with B =ᵐ[μ] B₀ (NullMeasurableSet). Then μ(B) = μ(B₀) (measure_congr). The set (B ∩ M) Δ (B₀ ∩ M) is contained in {x : x ∈ B ↮ x ∈ B₀} ∩ M, a μ-null subset of M, hence H^n-null by 2; therefore B ∩ M =ᵐ[H^n] B₀ ∩ M, H^n.restrict (B ∩ M) = H^n.restrict (B₀ ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_congr_set), and by 9, ∫⁻_{B ∩ M} ENNReal.ofReal θ dH^n = ∫⁻_{B₀ ∩ M} ENNReal.ofReal θ dH^n = μ(B₀) = μ(B).

11. Integrability (a). Let K ⊆ U be compact. M ∩ K is H^n-null-measurable and θ = (Θ̂ ·).toReal on M ∩ K (1), so θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n.restrict (M ∩ K). Since θ > 0 on M, ∫⁻_{M ∩ K} ‖θ‖ₑ dH^n = ∫⁻_{K ∩ M} ENNReal.ofReal θ dH^n = μ(K) < ∞ by 9 applied to the Borel set K. Hence IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) μHE[n]. ∎

μ_V-null subsets of M are H^n-null (frt_hausdorff_null_of_weight_null).
Pieces M_p = {θ ≥ 1/p} ∩ K_p are null-measurable with H^n(M_p) < ∞ (Simon 3.3; atoms if n = 0).
λ_p = H^n⌞M_p has density one a.e. (frt_hausdorff_density_one_of_flat_covers); μ_V⌞M_p ≪ λ_p (frt_weight_null_of_hausdorff_null).
Besicovitch differentiation + Lebesgue density of M_p for μ_V: d(μ_V⌞M_p)/dλ_p = θ λ_p-a.e., so μ_V⌞M_p = θ H^n⌞M_p.
Monotone limit p → ∞ gives μ_V(B) = ∫_{B∩M} θ dH^n for Borel B; extend to μ_V-null-measurable B via step 2.
Integrability on M ∩ K from μ_V(K) < ∞ and the Borel representative.

If V has a tangent plane in the sense of Def. 1.1 at μ_V-a.e. x, then for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^N × G(N,n) the set S_A := {x : ∃ T θ, HasTangentPlane V x T θ ∧ (x, T) ∈ A} is μ_V-null-measurable and V(A) = μ_V(S_A).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, printed proof of Theorem 1.2 (p. 208), second paragraph: "if x ∈ M is one of the μ_V-almost all points such that η_V^(x) exists, and if β is a non-negative continuous function on G(n + ℓ, n), then we evidently have η_V^(x)(β) = θ(x)β(T_x) and hence by the second part of 1.3 we have (1) ∫_{Gₙ(A)} β(S) dV(x, S) = ∫_{M∩A} β(T_x) dμ_V(x) for any Borel set A ⊆ U. From the arbitrariness of A and β it then easily follows that (2) ∫ f(x, S) dV(x, S) = ∫_M f(x, T_x) dμ_V(x) for any non-negative f ∈ C_c(Gₙ(U))." ERRATUM (documented in the parent proof): the printed "η_V^(x)(β) = θ(x)β(T_x)" must read "η_V^(x)(β) = β(T_x)"; the averages in Lemma 1.3 are normalised by μ_V(B_ρ(x)), so the multiplicity cancels, and the printed (1) is consistent only with the corrected value. The details below are Step 8 of the parent proof. Notation: μ := V.weight; G := Grassmannian N n (a compact metrizable space; we use the Frobenius distance d(S, S') := (Σ_{a,b} (S_{ab} − S'_{ab})²)^{1/2} of the matrices, which induces its topology); B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ; Gₙ(A) := A ×ˢ univ; ω := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞); H^n := μHE[n]; for continuous β on G and ρ > 0, avg_ρ^x(β) := (∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x))} β(S) dV) / μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal (the quotient in the hypothesis).

0. Degenerate case. If G = ∅ (n > N), then {x : ∃ T θ, HasTangentPlane V x T θ} = ∅ and the a.e. hypothesis gives μ(ℝ^N) = 0; moreover ℝ^N × G is empty, so V.measure = 0. Then every set is μ-null-measurable and V(A) = 0 = μ(S_A). Assume G ≠ ∅ and fix S₀ ∈ G.

1. Tangent data. By frt_tangent_plane_unique, at a tangent point x the plane and multiplicity are unique; write T(x), θ(x) (θ(x) > 0). Let X be the set of tangent points x at which the first clause of the hypothesis on η holds (η(x) is a probability measure and avg_ρ^x(β) → ∫ β dη(x) for all β ∈ C(G)). Both clauses hold μ-a.e., so μ(ℝ^N ∖ X) = 0.

2. Averages at a tangent point. Let x be a tangent point with plane T and multiplicity θ > 0. Claim: avg_ρ^x(β) → β(T) as ρ ↓ 0, for every β ∈ C(G).
 (a) Denominator: by frt_tangent_plane_hasDensity, μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω ρ^n) → θ, so ρ^{−n} μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal → θ ω.toReal > 0 (and μ(B_ρ(x)) ∈ (0, ∞) for small ρ; x ∈ U and U is open, so closedBall x (2ρ) ⊆ U is compact and V(B_{2ρ}(x) × G) = μ(B_{2ρ}(x)) < ∞ for small ρ).
 (b) Numerator for β ≥ 0: for χ ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, the function f_χ(y, S) := χ(y) β(S) lies in C_c(ℝ^N × G) (G compact). For ρ > 0, rescaledMeasure V x ρ = ENNReal.ofReal(ρ⁻¹ ^ n) • V.measure.map φ_ρ with φ_ρ(y, S) := (ρ⁻¹ • (y − x), S) continuous, so by integral_smul_measure ((ENNReal.ofReal(ρ⁻¹ ^ n)).toReal = ρ⁻¹ ^ n) and integral_map (f_χ continuous), ∫ f_χ d(rescaledMeasure V x ρ) = ρ⁻¹ ^ n ∫ χ(ρ⁻¹ • (y − x)) β(S) dV(y, S); and planeVarifoldMeasure T = (H^n.restrict T.plane).map (y ↦ (y, T)), so by integral_map, ∫ f_χ d(planeVarifoldMeasure T) = ∫_{T.plane} χ(y) β(T) dH^n(y) = β(T) ∫_{T.plane} χ dH^n. By HasTangentPlane, ρ^{−n} ∫ χ(ρ⁻¹ • (y − x)) β(S) dV → θ β(T) ∫_{T.plane} χ dH^n. Use the cutoffs χ_{a,b}(y) := max(0, min(1, (b − |y|)/(b − a))) for 0 < a < b (continuous, 0 ≤ χ_{a,b} ≤ 1, χ_{a,b} = 1 on B_a(0), χ_{a,b} = 0 outside ball 0 b, so χ_{a,b} ∈ C_c(ℝ^N)). For κ ∈ (0, 1): χ_{1−κ,1}(ρ⁻¹ • (y − x)) ≤ 1_{B_ρ(x)}(y) ≤ χ_{1,1+κ}(ρ⁻¹ • (y − x)) for all y, so (β ≥ 0; all integrals are finite for small ρ, the integrands being bounded and supported in B_{2ρ}(x) × G)
 ρ^{−n} ∫ χ_{1−κ,1}(ρ⁻¹(y − x)) β(S) dV ≤ ρ^{−n} ∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x))} β dV ≤ ρ^{−n} ∫ χ_{1,1+κ}(ρ⁻¹(y − x)) β(S) dV.
 The outer terms tend to θβ(T)∫_{T.plane} χ_{1−κ,1} dH^n ≥ θ β(T) ω.toReal (1 − κ)^n and to θβ(T)∫_{T.plane} χ_{1,1+κ} dH^n ≤ θ β(T) ω.toReal (1 + κ)^n respectively, using 1_{B_{1−κ}(0)} ≤ χ_{1−κ,1}, χ_{1,1+κ} ≤ 1_{B_{1+κ}(0)}, β(T) ≥ 0 and H^n(T.plane ∩ B_s(0)) = ω s^n for s > 0 (via a linear isometry ℝ^n → T.plane: Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Measure.addHaar_closedBall; for n = 0 both sides equal 1). Hence θβ(T)ω.toReal(1 − κ)^n ≤ liminf_{ρ↓0} ρ^{−n} ∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x))} β dV ≤ limsup_{ρ↓0} ρ^{−n} ∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x))} β dV ≤ θβ(T)ω.toReal(1 + κ)^n for every κ ∈ (0, 1); letting κ → 0 gives ρ^{−n} ∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x))} β dV → θ ω.toReal β(T).
 (c) General β ∈ C(G): β = β⁺ − β⁻ with β^± := max(±β, 0) ∈ C(G), β^± ≥ 0; by linearity of the (finite) integrals, ρ^{−n} ∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x))} β dV → θ ω.toReal β(T).
 (d) Dividing (c) by (a): avg_ρ^x(β) → θ ω.toReal β(T)/(θ ω.toReal) = β(T). (This is the corrected printed claim η_V^(x)(β) = β(T_x).)

3. η is Dirac. For x ∈ X, by the hypothesis and 2, ∫ β dη(x) = β(T(x)) for every β ∈ C(G) (uniqueness of limits along 𝓝[>] 0). η(x) and the Dirac measure δ_{T(x)} are finite Borel measures on the compact metrizable space G with equal integrals of all continuous functions, hence equal (both are regular, and Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported applies since C_c(G) = C(G)). In particular ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal β dη(x) = ENNReal.ofReal (β(T(x))) for β ≥ 0.

4. A Borel version of T. For matrix indices a, b let e_{ab}(S) := S.1 a b, a continuous function on G. For k ≥ 1 the function a_k^{ab}(x) := (∫_{Gₙ(B_{1/k}(x))} e_{ab}(S) dV) / μ(B_{1/k}(x)).toReal is Borel in x: x ↦ μ(B_{1/k}(x)) is Borel (Mathlib measurable_measure_prodMk_left for the s-finite μ and the closed set {(x, y) : dist y x ≤ 1/k}, whose section at x is B_{1/k}(x)), and x ↦ ∫ 1_{|y − x| ≤ 1/k} e_{ab}(S) dV(y, S) is Borel by measurability of parametric integrals of jointly Borel functions for the σ-finite measure V.measure (Varifold.measure.instSigmaFinite; e.g. MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right' applied to (x, (y, S)) ↦ 1_{dist y x ≤ 1/k} e_{ab}(S), the set {dist y x ≤ 1/k} being closed). For x ∈ X, a_k^{ab}(x) → ∫ e_{ab} dη(x) = T(x).1 a b as k → ∞ (hypothesis along ρ = 1/k → 0⁺, and 3). Let Y be the Borel set of x at which every sequence (a_k^{ab}(x))_k converges and the matrix of limits is symmetric, idempotent and has trace n (i.e. lies in G, a closed set of matrices); put T̃(x) := that matrix for x ∈ Y and T̃(x) := S₀ otherwise. Then T̃ : ℝ^N → G is Borel, X ⊆ Y and T̃ = T on X; so T̃(x) = T(x) for μ-a.e. x.

5. Identity (1). For Borel A' ⊆ ℝ^N and β ∈ C(G) with β ≥ 0, by the second hypothesis on η, 3 and 4,
 ∫⁻_{Gₙ(A')} ENNReal.ofReal β(S) dV = ∫⁻_{A'} ∫⁻ ENNReal.ofReal β dη(x) dμ(x) = ∫⁻_{A'} ENNReal.ofReal β(T̃(x)) dμ(x),
 the integrands agreeing on the full-measure set X (lintegral_congr_ae).

6. Rectangles. Let ν := μ.map (x ↦ (x, T̃(x))) (a Borel map), so ν(A' × B) = μ(A' ∩ T̃⁻¹(B)) for Borel A', B. Let K_m (m ≥ 1) be a compact exhaustion of U: K_m := closedBall 0 m if U = ℝ^N, and otherwise K_m := {x : |x| ≤ m and infDist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) ≥ 1/m}; each K_m is compact, K_m ⊆ K_{m+1} ⊆ U and ⋃_m K_m = U (for x ∈ U, infDist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) > 0 as ℝ^N ∖ U is closed). G carries no MetricSpace instance, so fix explicitly the Frobenius distance d(S, S') := (Σ_{a,b} (S.1 a b − S'.1 a b)²)^{1/2}, a continuous function on G × G inducing the subspace topology of G (alternatively, any metric given by TopologicalSpace.metrizableSpaceMetric). Let A' ⊆ K_m be Borel and F ⊆ G closed. If F = ∅ then V(A' × F) = 0 = ν(A' × F). Otherwise d_F(S) := inf_{S' ∈ F} d(S, S') is continuous and, F being compact, d_F(S) = 0 ⟺ S ∈ F; put β_j(S) := max(0, 1 − j · d_F(S)). Then β_j ∈ C(G), 0 ≤ β_j ≤ 1 and β_j ↓ 1_F pointwise. By 5, ∫⁻_{Gₙ(A')} β_j(S) dV = ∫⁻_{A'} β_j(T̃(x)) dμ(x); both sides are bounded by V(K_m × G) = μ(K_m) < ∞, so letting j → ∞ (monotone convergence for decreasing sequences with finite integrals, or dominated convergence) gives V(A' × F) = μ(A' ∩ T̃⁻¹(F)) = ν(A' × F). For fixed A', B ↦ V(A' × B) and B ↦ ν(A' × B) are finite Borel measures on G that agree on the closed sets, a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra of G and containing G itself; hence they agree on every Borel B ⊆ G (MeasureTheory.ext_of_generate_finite). For Borel A' ⊆ ℝ^N ∖ U: V(A' × B) ≤ V(Uᶜ × G) = 0 (V.supported) and ν(A' × B) ≤ μ(A') ≤ μ(Uᶜ) = V(Uᶜ × G) = 0 (Varifold.weight_apply).

7. V = ν (printed (2)). Let 𝓒 be the family of rectangles A' × B with B ⊆ G Borel and A' ⊆ ℝ^N Borel such that A' ⊆ K_m for some m or A' ⊆ ℝ^N ∖ U. 𝓒 is closed under finite intersections (a π-system). Every Borel rectangle A' × B is the countable union ((A' ∖ U) × B) ∪ ⋃_m ((A' ∩ K_m) × B) of members of 𝓒, and Borel rectangles generate the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^N × G (both factors are second countable: Prod.borelSpace / generateFrom_prod), so 𝓒 generates it as well. By 6, V.measure and ν agree on 𝓒, and the sets K_m × G (finite V- and ν-measure, V(K_m × G) = μ(K_m) = ν(K_m × G)) together with (ℝ^N ∖ U) × G (measure 0) form a countable cover of ℝ^N × G by members of 𝓒 of finite measure. By Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion (Mathlib MeasureTheory/Measure/Restrict.lean:491), V.measure = ν.

8. Conclusion. Let A ⊆ ℝ^N × G be Borel and Ã := {x : (x, T̃(x)) ∈ A}, a Borel set. By 7 and Measure.map_apply, V(A) = ν(A) = μ(Ã). For x ∈ X we have x ∈ S_A ⟺ x ∈ Ã: if HasTangentPlane V x T θ and (x, T) ∈ A then T = T(x) = T̃(x) by frt_tangent_plane_unique and 4; conversely, if (x, T̃(x)) ∈ A then HasTangentPlane V x T(x) θ(x) with T(x) = T̃(x) and (x, T(x)) ∈ A. Hence S_A and Ã differ only inside the μ-null set ℝ^N ∖ X, i.e. S_A =ᵐ[μ] Ã; so S_A is μ-null-measurable and μ(S_A) = μ(Ã) = V(A). ∎
proof_key_steps: G = ∅ is trivial; otherwise X = {tangent points where Lemma 1.3(i) holds} has full μ_V-measure.
At a tangent point, cutoff squeezes give (∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x))} β dV)/μ_V(B_ρ(x)) → β(T_x) (corrected η_V^(x)(β) = β(T_x)).
Hence η(x) = δ_{T(x)} on X, and Lemma 1.3(ii) gives (1): ∫_{Gₙ(A')} β dV = ∫_{A'} β(T̃(x)) dμ_V with a Borel T̃ = T μ_V-a.e. built from averages of matrix entries.
V and ν := μ_V.map(x ↦ (x, T̃ x)) agree on rectangles A' × B (closed B by approximation, then all Borel B).
π-system of rectangles over the compact exhaustion and Uᶜ: V = ν (printed (2)).
V(A) = μ_V{x : (x,T̃x) ∈ A}, which equals μ_V(S_A) because S_A =ᵐ that Borel set (uniqueness of tangent planes).

audit.reason: The corrected cutoff squeeze gives the normalized limit β(T), so the disintegration measures are Dirac almost everywhere. Matrix-entry averages provide a Borel plane representative. Finite-localization rectangle uniqueness proves the graph-measure identity, and tangent uniqueness gives the stated null-measurable existential set. The empty Grassmannian case is handled.
